Table 3: Overall benchmark of 19 segmentation models on RadGenome-Anatomy. Each cell is reported as mean ± 95% CI half-width from bootstrap resampling over classes. ↑ indicates higher is better, and ↓ indicates lower is better. Best results are shown in bold.
Figure 1: Comparison between conventional 2D manual annotation and our volumetric-toradiographic annotation paradigm.

Figure 4: Per-class Dice performance for selected L3 anatomical classes in PA and LL views (see Table A6 for exact values). The left panel reports the PA view, and the right panel reports the LL view. In each panel, the x-axis indexes anatomical classes, grouped by anatomical system, and the y-axis shows Dice score. For each class, points denote model performance values, the central curve shows the mean Dice across models, and the upper and lower curves show mean ± one standard deviation.

Figure 6: Quantitative evaluation of mask-derived measurement-based screening for cardiomegaly, kyphosis, and scoliosis. Each row corresponds to one condition. From left to right, the panels show the cohort summary and headline metrics, binary positive vs. negative performance, ordinal severity performance, per-class precision/recall/F1, row-normalised confusion matrix, and the distribution of the underlying continuous measurement across ground-truth severity grades.

Figure 2: Hierarchical label space and anatomy-mask scale in RadGenome-Anatomy. a. Fourlevel sunburst of the 210 canonical anatomy classes. The innermost ring shows the 10 body-system groups, while the outer rings progressively expand the hierarchy into organ families, anatomical sub-parts, and the final canonical classes (Detailed label hierarchy is provided in Figure A4.). b. Anatomy-mask area for each body-system group. Error bars indicate 95% bootstrap CIs.

Figure 7: Qualitative examples of diagnostic measurements derived from XAnatomy-predicted anatomy masks. Columns present cases spanning negative, mild, moderate, and severe categories, while rows correspond to cardiomegaly, thoracic kyphosis, and scoliosis.

Figure 3: Overview of the volumetric-to-radiographic projection pipeline. A preprocessed 3D CT volume V and anatomy-specific 3D masks {M (c)}Cc=1 are projected into postero-anterior (PA) and lateral (LL) views.
